# Fanqie original text source

This directory contains an independent copy of the MIT Muse Fanqie free-reading engine and its vendored MIT primitives. The data station never imports Muse packages, reads Muse user data, or requires a Muse process. `SOURCE.json` records the copied engine digest and upstream manifests; `engine.py` remains unchanged. `worker.py` owns one normal anonymous reading client per book, validates fixed official HTTPS sources, spaces requests, and returns only the requested directory or chapter over bounded JSON lines. Device identifiers and negotiated keys remain in worker memory and are not logged.

Run `node scripts/setup-novel-runtime.mjs` from the project to create `.data/novel-runtime` and install the pinned `pycryptodome==3.23.0` dependency. `--python /absolute/python3` selects the interpreter used to create this private environment. Python needs a functioning TLS trust store. `createFanqieNovelSource` accepts an explicit `caFile` when the interpreter's default CA location is missing; certificate verification remains enabled. No global Python packages or Muse runtime files are used. The setup script accepts only the standard network proxy and CA environment variables in addition to PATH; worker children receive PATH, the explicitly configured CA file, and proxy variables only when `networkMode=system` is selected.

The adapter requires absolute `sourceDirectory` pointing to this project's `third_party/fanqie-original`, absolute `workerDirectory` below this project's `.data`, absolute `pythonExecutable`, `requestTimeoutMs`, `requestIntervalMs`, `maxResponseBytes`, `maxChapterBytes`, `callTimeoutMs`, `graceMs`, and `networkMode`. Worker paths are explicit so bundled server code does not depend on source-directory depth. Runtime directories reject symbolic links. The adapter cross-checks every website chapter ID, index, title and total against the normal reading API directory; any paid, locked or paid-publication/story chapter prevents body retrieval. It does not decode font-masked website bodies, bypass locked content, or use third-party text mirrors.

The website's `page.status` is the serial status (`1` ongoing, `2` finished); `page.creationStatus` is a different field and must not determine completion. Chapter references remain canonical `https://fanqienovel.com/reader/<id>` URLs. Source word counts remain separate from returned text lengths; missing counts are null, and returned non-whitespace character counts must meet every declared count. Invalid identities, missing chapters, masked or replacement characters, short previews, malformed protocol frames, process errors and incomplete stream termination cannot publish an original-text file. The owning novel library persists chapter checkpoints and publishes immutable files only after a complete directory and successful worker release.

Run `pnpm exec vitest run tests/fanqie-original.test.ts` for adapter, website, protocol, environment and process-lifecycle cases. After setting up the private runtime, run `.data/novel-runtime/bin/python3 -I -B third_party/fanqie-original/test_worker.py` for offline free-reading validation, including authorization, exact identities, complete directories and truncated bodies. The Windows runtime path is `.data/novel-runtime/Scripts/python.exe`.

Native qualification on 2026-11-13 used the official short-text candidate `7395464458719464510` (`三字经`), whose official directory had two unlocked, unpaid chapters. The website and normal anonymous reading API agreed on both chapter identities and order. The returned original body had 1922 non-whitespace characters against the source's 1922-character declaration. Its UTF-8 SHA256 was `e8f7aac9bf565eb6250c2ef34610718221800db87c1f1f4b729b3540d3efba78`. Only counts and hashes were recorded in the ignored native receipt; no device information, keys or novel text were printed. This qualifies that source and directory at that time, not unrestricted access to other books or future platform behavior.
